the_signal.headline: On-device LLMs hit 24B sweet spot for production agents
the_signal.body: Liquid AI's LFM2.5-24B-A2B is built specifically for fast on-device agents — this means GTM workflows no longer need cloud roundtrips for every decision. Lower latency, lower cost per inference, and no API rate limits: this is the architecture shift that makes embedded revenue systems actually deployable at scale.

tool_drop.name: Jev 1.14.0
tool_drop.what: Type-safe AI workflow framework now shipping experimental features for agent state management and multi-step reasoning.
tool_drop.why: GTM engineers need deterministic, testable agent behavior — Jev's type safety catches workflow bugs before they hit production and tank your conversion pipeline.

thread_of_day.title: API Contract Testing Prevents Production Failures
thread_of_day.takeaway: Validating API responses mid-workflow execution catches breaking changes before they cascade through your revenue automation — not after your SDR workflow silently fails.

quote.text: Every weekday at 8am, this workflow searches the day's AI news, scores every article for materiality at about $0.00004 apiece, and posts one cited brief per topic to Slack.

whats_moving.context: AWS Labs released adaptive workflow rules for AI coding agents — this pattern is now spreading to revenue workflows where intent-to-execution needs guard rails.

whats_moving.topic: Knowledge graphs vs. vector RAG trade-offs
whats_moving.context: n8n's comparison guide signals that GTM teams need to choose grounding strategy based on determinism vs. flexibility — vector RAG wins for discovery, knowledge graphs win for repeatable qualification.
